blockingLoop.evidence: Second reply is a verbatim repeat of the first: 'Stop using this appliance ... switch it off at the wall or the fuse box only if you can do that safely, get everyone out and call 999.' despite the customer asking a direct question.

rationale: The core emergency advice was correct and safe: keep the door shut, switch off at the wall only if safe, get out and call 999, with no unsafe instruction (no opening the door, no water). However the assistant never engaged with what the customer said: when told 'door is closed ... should i switch it off at the wall? the socket is to the side, away from the flames' it simply pasted the identical boilerplate card again rather than confirming 'yes, switch it off now' or checking whether flames were spreading or dying down. No cause was identified and no aftercare was given (ventilate, do not reuse, tell the landlord), so the homeowner got a safe but impersonal and repetitive response.
